[[Image:CMSAnotext 194x171.png|right]]
The '''Combinatorial Mathematics Society of Australasia (CMSA)''' is a professional society of [[mathematician]]s working in the field of [[combinatorics]].<ref name=EAS>{{cite web | title = Combinatorial Mathematics Society of Australasia | publisher = Encyclopedia of Australian Science | url = http://www.eoas.info/biogs/A002175b.htm | access-date = May 1, 2017}}</ref> It is the primary combinatorics society for [[Australasia]], consisting of [[Australia]], [[New Zealand]] and neighbouring countries. The CMSA existed as an informal group from 1972 until formal establishment in 1978. It became an incorporated association in 1996, and as of 2017, it has over 280 members including 110 life members.<ref name=History>{{cite web | publisher = CMSA | title = About the society | url =  http://combinatorics-australasia.org/index.html | access-date = May 1, 2017}}</ref>

==Membership and management==

The membership of the CMSA consists of four classes: ordinary members, honorary members, institutional members, and life members.<ref name=Admin>{{cite web | publisher = CMSA | title = Rules of the Combinatorial Mathematics Society of Australasia Incorporated | url = http://combinatorics-australasia.org/rules/CMSA-Rules.pdf | access-date = April 29, 2017}}</ref>

The CMSA Council is responsible for all activities of the Society. It consists of a president, vice-president, immediate past president (if there is one), secretary, treasurer, and a number of other members elected by members of the CMSA at its Annual General Meeting.

===CMSA presidents===
Presidents of the CMSA are shown below.<ref name=Presidents>{{cite web | publisher = CMSA | title = Council | url = http://combinatorics-australasia.org/council.html | access-date = September 2, 2026}}</ref> 
* [[Anne Penfold Street]] (1997–98)
* Derek Holton (1999–2001)
* [[Nick Wormald]] (2002–03)
* [[Brendan McKay (mathematician)|Brendan McKay]] (2004)
* Paul Bonnington (2005–06)
* [[Ian Wanless]] (2007–09)
* Robert Aldred (2010)
* [[Catherine Greenhill]] (2011–13)
* [[Ian Wanless]] (2014)
* David Wood (2015–16)
* Sanming Zhou (2017)
* Jeanette McLeod (2018–20)
* [[Brendan McKay (mathematician)|Brendan McKay]] (2021)
* Thomas Britz (2022–2024)
* [[Ian Wanless]] (2025)
* Binzhou Xia (2026)

==Activities==

The main activities of the CMSA are to publish the [[Australasian Journal of Combinatorics]] (AJC),<ref name=AJC>{{cite web | publisher = Australasian Journal of Combinatorics | title = About the Journal | url = https://ajc.maths.uq.edu.au/ | access-date = April 28, 2017}}</ref> and to oversee the organisation of the annual Australasian Conference on Combinatorial Mathematics and Combinatorial Computing (ACCMCC), and the ten-yearly International Combinatorics Conference (ICC).<ref name=Conferences>{{cite web | publisher = CMSA | title = Conferences | url =  http://combinatorics-australasia.org/conferences.html | access-date = April 28, 2017}}</ref> The CMSA also publishes an E-Newsletter in April, July, and October each year.<ref name=Newsletters>{{cite web | publisher = CMSA | title = CMSA E-Newsletters | url =  http://combinatoricswiki.org/wiki/Combinatorial_Mathematics_Society_of_Australasia_Newsletters | access-date = April 30, 2017}}</ref>

===Student support===
The CMSA strongly encourages student participation in its conferences. The ''CMSA Student Support Scheme'' provides travel support, and the ''CMSA Anne Penfold Street Student Prize'' (formerly called the ''CMSA Student Prize'', 2001–16) is awarded annually for the best student talk.<ref name=Students>{{cite web | publisher = CMSA | title = CMSA Student Support | url = http://combinatorics-australasia.org/students.html | access-date = April 29, 2017}}</ref>

==CMSA Medal==

The CMSA Medal is awarded at most every three years, to honour a member of the CMSA who has made outstanding and sustained contributions to combinatorics and to the Australasian combinatorics community.<ref name=Medal>{{cite web | publisher = CMSA | title = CMSA Medal | url = http://combinatorics-australasia.org/medal.html | access-date = April 28, 2017}}</ref>

The following individuals have been awarded the CMSA Medal:<ref name=Medal/>
* [[Anne Penfold Street]] (1999)
* Derek Holton (2005)
* [[Jennifer Seberry]] (2008)
* Elizabeth Billington (2011)
* [[Brendan McKay (mathematician)|Brendan McKay]] (2014)
* Darryn Bryant (2019)
* [[Ian Wanless]] (2022)
* [[Nick Wormald]] (2025)

==CMSA Prize==

The CMSA Prize is awarded for excellence in a single body of research in combinatorial mathematics.<ref name=Prize>{{cite web | publisher = CMSA | title = CMSA Medal | url = http://combinatorics-australasia.org/prize.html | access-date = April 28, 2017}}</ref>

The following individuals have been awarded the CMSA Prize.<ref name=Prize/>
* Nina Kamčev (2023)
